paragraphs: Art. 2. (1) By the agricultural lease contract, the lessor undertakes to give the object of the contract to the lessee for temporary use, and the lessee undertakes to make a specific lease payment.
(2) The yields from the leased objects become the property of the lessee from the moment they are separated.

Art. 3. (1) Agricultural lease contracts, and the agreements to change or to end them, are concluded in writing, with a notarial certification of the signatures of the parties made at the same time. In the notarial procedure, the notary checks that the requirements of para. 4 are met and keeps sketches of the plots that are the object of the contract. The notary requests the sketches by remote access to the information system of the cadastre and the property register, or a party provides them in the notarial procedure. When there is no cadastral map and no cadastral registers in force for the land area, the notary keeps sketches of the plots issued by the municipal agricultural office where the plots are.

(2) Agricultural lease contracts, and the agreements to change or to end them, concluded in writing with a notarial certification of the signatures of the parties, are entered in the registry office and registered in the municipal agricultural office. The sketches of the plots obtained under para. 1 are attached to the act for entry.
(3) For the registration of agricultural lease contracts in the municipal agricultural offices, the rules of Art. 37b(7) of the Ownership and Use of Agricultural Land Act apply.

(4) An agricultural lease contract, and an agreement to change or to end it, may be concluded with an owner, or with a co-owner of agricultural land who owns more than 50 per cent of the ideal parts of a co-owned plot, or with a person authorised by an owner or by co-owners who, together with that person, hold more than 50 per cent of the ideal parts of the co-owned plot. The authorisation must be an express power of attorney with a notarially certified signature. In these cases, the relations between the co-owners are governed by Art. 30(3) of the Ownership Act.
(5) (Repealed.)
Art. 4. (1) The minimum term of an agricultural lease contract is five business years.

Art. 18. (1) The extension of an agricultural lease contract is made in writing with a notarial certification of the signatures, and is entered in the registry offices and in the register of the municipal agricultural office.
(2) The proposal to extend the contract must be made at the latest by the end of the ninth month of the business year before the end of the agricultural lease contract.
Art. 27. (1) An agricultural lease contract ends:
1. when the term for which it was concluded expires;
2. on non-performance, by the general procedure, unless this act provides otherwise;
3. by mutual consent of the parties, expressed in writing with a notarial certification of the signatures;
4. by a unilateral notice, in the cases that this act provides;

5. apart from other reasons named in the law, also by the death or the placement under interdiction of the lessee, or by the end of the legal entity that is the lessee, unless the contract provides otherwise;
6. on the expropriation of leased land for state and municipal needs under Chapter Three of the State Property Act and of the Municipal Property Act.
(2) The end of an agricultural lease contract for land is entered in the registry office and registered in the municipal agricultural office.
